rationale.conceptual: The method is a standard quantum chemical procedure (UHF/6-31G* geometry optimisation) applied to small organic molecules. No novel algorithms or deep theoretical derivations are required; it is a routine use of an established method. However, it is not a trivial textbook operation like computing a mean, as it demands correct selection of protonation sites, proper setup of ab initio calculations, and interpretation of electronic energies.
rationale.execution: The workflow consists of 5 stages: neutral optimisations, protonated-species optimisations, PA computation, dipole extraction, and most-favourable-site determination. All steps use a single standard tool (Psi4) and involve straightforward I/O. No complex data acquisition or environment setup is needed; the pipeline is linear and uncomplicated.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper uses standard Hartree-Fock/6-31G* calculations on small molecules to compute proton affinities. The method is a textbook application of ab initio quantum chemistry, requiring no novel algorithms. The pipeline involves multiple geometry optimisations but uses a standard open-source package (Psi4) and straightforward data processing; no tricky orchestration or large data. Resource needs are minimal: CPU-only, tiny RAM, no external datasets.
